USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Reduced antibiotic exposure with antacids

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 42-year-old woman takes prescribed oral ciprofloxacin at the same time as a magnesium-aluminum antacid. A medication review identifies unexpectedly low antibiotic exposure despite adherence and normal kidney function. Which interaction most plausibly accounts for the reduced exposure?

  1. Irreversible inhibition of bacterial drug uptake
  2. Formation of poorly absorbed complexes in the intestinal lumen
  3. Induction of hepatic enzymes that metabolize ciprofloxacin
  4. Increased renal tubular secretion of ciprofloxacin
  5. Displacement of ciprofloxacin from albumin into tissues
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Formation of poorly absorbed complexes in the intestinal lumen

Multivalent cations can complex with ciprofloxacin and reduce its gastrointestinal absorption.

Understanding the options

Formation of poorly absorbed complexes in the intestinal lumen
Luminal complex formation reduces the amount absorbed.
Induction of hepatic enzymes that metabolize ciprofloxacin
This interaction is primarily absorptive, not enzyme induction.
Increased renal tubular secretion of ciprofloxacin
The antacid does not principally act by accelerating renal secretion.
Displacement of ciprofloxacin from albumin into tissues
Protein-binding displacement does not explain reduced oral absorption.
Irreversible inhibition of bacterial drug uptake
A bacterial uptake change would not directly lower measured systemic drug exposure.
